name: Sonsign
image_type: Sonsign / pure actual sound situation (zeroness of the time-image, sound side)
definition: The actual sound image cut off from its motor extension: a sound that is itself the situation rather than score, dialogue or cue for action. It is heard and holds the scene, while neither the listener nor the image converts it into a response. It is the aural twin of the opsign and can occur without one, over a neutral image, a frozen listener or black.
deamer_quote: ‘actual on-screen de-differenciated visual and audio images’ (p.138)
deleuze_examples: Mr. Hulot's Holiday / Playtime (Jacques Tati, 1953 / 1967): noises such as the flapping dining-room door and the buzzing, clicking modern building stand as situations in their own right (recalled from Cinema 2, ch.1; not in Deamer)
India Song (Marguerite Duras, 1975): voices off, never synchronised with the bodies on screen, form a sound situation of their own (recalled from Cinema 2, ch.9; not in Deamer)
Fortini/Cani (Jean-Marie Straub and Daniele Huillet, 1976): a text read aloud over empty landscapes, the speech act kept apart from the visual layer (recalled from Cinema 2, ch.9; not in Deamer)

Umberto D. (Vittorio De Sica, 1952): the maid's morning kitchen, where tap, coffee grinder and door noises carry no action (recalled from Cinema 2, ch.1; Deleuze stresses the optical side there; not in Deamer)
deleuze_examples_source: Deamer's Section II (pp.138-144) cites no films and treats opsigns and sonsigns jointly; these examples are recalled from Deleuze's Cinema 2 and should be checked against it. The split of sonsign into its own element is this project's, not Deamer's.

scenes: On the promenade, four old men with canes stop to talk, but their speech is never heard. The roar of the breaking waves takes its place, so the talk turns into a sound situation with no content (p.302).

The white noise of the sea runs through the first four sequences as a constant bed, including the one where the dogs lie on the beach and the light bleaches out. It is an environment you hear and never a cue (p.304).

'Moon on Water, Serenade of Toads' opens in near silence on a black screen. A slow crescendo of toads and a storm builds 'in time' into the roar of nature, and it grows on its own while the image has nearly vanished (p.304).
Plops of raindrops and lightning hit the black water and blur the moon's reflection, so the sound of the storm stands in for any event (p.304).

operation: Take away the action and let a sound hold the scene: starve the image, or freeze the listener, until what is heard is the situation instead of an accompaniment or a signal to act.
shot_criteria: From the image alone (visual search), look for either (a) a listener frozen before an unseen or distant source, head tilted or turned, not moving to answer, or (b) a sound source isolated with no action attached: bells, loudspeakers, radio, phonograph, sirens, whistles, machinery running unattended, rain on water, surf, frogs or birds calling, crowds heard off an empty frame. It can also be a near-empty or dark image where sound would have to carry everything. After that, a listen must confirm three things: the sound stands alone (not music scoring, not dialogue driving plot), it goes on longer than any action it could trigger, and nobody responds to it.
queries: person standing motionless in a town square listening to a loudspeaker mounted on a pole
church bells swinging in a belfry, close shot, no people
family sitting still around a radio set in a living room, listening
steam whistle blowing on a factory roof, plume of steam, no workers
heavy rain falling onto a pond surface at night, ripples, fixed camera
phonograph horn playing in an empty room, record turning
frogs croaking at the edge of a pond, throat sacs swelling, close-up
telephone ringing unanswered on a desk in an empty office
waves breaking on rocks at a deserted shore, long static shot
people on a street looking up at the sky, listening to aircraft overhead
